title: The Winter Letter
premise: In the winter of 1794, as the Republic of Vessany collapses under its own army, courier Xanthe Underhill carries a ledger of names—debtors, dissidents, and the children they hid—into a garrison town where the military has come to requisition both the records and the people who kept them. Sheltered by an innkeeper's found family who once saved her life, she must choose between burning the ledger to protect them and smuggling it past three checkpoints to deliver it to the last honest magistrate before the century turns. Betrayed by the man she loves, who serves the very army hunting her, she trades her own name for the names in the book. The ledger reaches the magistrate; Xanthe does not escape with it, but survives, stripped of her old identity, to be claimed at last by the family that was never hers by blood.
about_author: Bram Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in provincial record offices. They write historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Xanthe arrives in the river town of Callowmere posing as a stationer's widow, the ledger sewn into a bolt of linen. Through her wary POV we learn how seven years of silence have taught her to read rooms. When she hears drums across the ice—the army is coming early—the emotional beat is dread: invisibility has an expiration date.

chapters.title: The Lamplighters' Table
chapters.summary: At the inn called the Second Bell, innkeeper Marta Voss folds Xanthe into a household of strays: a defrocked schoolmaster, twin ferry orphans, a deaf clockmaker. Xanthe's POV shows her resisting warmth out of habit. The beat is reluctant belonging—she catches herself laughing for the first time in years, and it terrifies her.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Colonel Aldous Rennick's troops occupy Callowmere and seal the records house, where the master ledger mirrors Xanthe's hidden one. From Rennick's POV we see a bureaucrat of cruelty who believes order is mercy. The beat is claustrophobic tightening: the town's fate and Xanthe's cargo are now the same paperwork.

chapters.title: A Man in a Grey Coat
chapters.summary: Lieutenant Elias Thorne, Rennick's adjutant and Xanthe's lover from the war years, recognizes her handwriting on a shipping manifest. Alternating POVs trace their charged reunion in the inn's cellar. The beat is love against duty: each realizes the other is now the greatest threat they face, and neither can say so aloud.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: The clockmaker reveals a smugglers' route beneath the frozen river, but using it means trusting the twins to run messages past sentries. Xanthe's POV weighs every name in the ledger like ballast. The beat is costly hope: the household votes to help her, making them all guilty, and she understands she has made them targets.

chapters.title: The First Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Disguised as a corpse-wagon driver, Xanthe moves the ledger through the bridge gate inside a coffin of schoolbooks. A routine inspection turns lethal when a guard recognizes the schoolmaster's hand on a forged pass. The beat is grief and resolve: the first crossing succeeds, but the pass betrays that someone inside the walls is helping her.

chapters.title: Confessions at the Second Bell
chapters.summary: Rennick orders the inn searched; Marta burns her late husband's letters to draw suspicion, sacrificing her last relic of him. Elias, ordered to interrogate the household, instead warns Xanthe in a coded lullaby. His POV breaks open: he chooses her over his oath. The beat is sacrifice compounding sacrifice, love declared in the grammar of treason.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Ledger
chapters.summary: Betrayed by the schoolmaster, who traded the route for his brother's pardon, Xanthe is captured at the second checkpoint—but Rennick finds only decoy pages. In custody she watches him realize the true ledger is already moving. The beat is the dark night: beaten and unnamed, she learns Elias took her place on the river road.

chapters.title: Three Bells Before Midnight
chapters.summary: Climax. On New Year's Eve, Elias runs the frozen river with the real ledger while Xanthe escapes custody to draw Rennick's riders after her across cracking ice. At the third checkpoint, the twins' ferry and the whole household converge. The beat is everything staked at once: she gives Rennick her true name to buy Elias the minutes he needs.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: The ledger reaches Magistrate Corven as church bells mark the new year; warrants dissolve, and the named are freed. Xanthe, officially dead under her old name, wakes in the Second Bell among people who refuse to let her vanish again. The beat is quiet resurrection: inheritance turns out not to be what we carry, but who claims us.
